original_question: Determine whether the vanishing micro-graphs that are indispensable for constructing and analyzing the dimension-(d+1) problem arise only by taking descendants of an underlying vanishing set already present in dimension d-1, rather than from genuinely new vanishing mechanisms appearing for the first time in higher dimension.
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting the third bullet in the paper’s final open-problems list: “Do these indispensable (cf. [6]) vanishing micro-graphs stem only from the underlying vanishing set in R^{d−1} through their descendants ?” This bullet is meant to be read together with the immediately preceding two bullets and with Proposition 1, which supplies the 3D→4D model case showing “no new (starting to work) mechanisms” in that specific step. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the core issue: the question is about vanishing Nambu micro-graphs that are needed in the dimensional step to d+1, whether they come from descendants of lower-dimensional vanishing data, and whether higher dimension introduces genuinely new vanishing behavior. It also correctly reflects the paper’s emphasis on “indispensable” vanishing graphs in the construction of the higher-dimensional trivializing problem.
missing_details: The paper is not asking this for arbitrary graph-theoretic or Poisson problems; it is specifically about the tetrahedral Kontsevich cocycle γ3 and the attempt to trivialize its flow on the Nambu–Poisson class. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))

The ambient geometric setting should be stated: the Nambu–Poisson brackets are the Jacobian-determinant brackets {f,g}d(x)=ρ(x)·det(∂(f,g,a1,…,a_{d−2})/∂(x1,…,xd))(x) on affine real space R^d, with Casimirs a1,…,a_{d−2} and inverse density ρ. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))

The relevant objects are vanishing 1-vector Nambu micro-graphs Γ, where vanishing means vanishing as formulas, i.e. φ(Γ)=0, not merely graph-theoretic zero. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))

The micro-graphs in the higher-dimensional trivialization problem are built from whole copies of bracket (1); in the tetrahedral case the paper uses micro-graphs with m=1 sink and n=3 copies of the Nambu bracket. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))

The notion of descendant must be made explicit: in the step d→d+1, one adjoins one new Casimir a_{d−1} to each Levi-Civita vertex, and every incoming edge that previously acted on a Casimir is expanded by the Leibniz rule over the old and new Casimir targets. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))

The paper distinguishes descendants from embeddings; an embedding adjoins the new Casimir but does not work out Leibniz rules. That distinction is part of the nearby context for the open problem. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))

The logical scope of the third bullet is conditional on the first two bullets: first, if the (d+1)-dimensional tetrahedral flow is trivial, so that Q^{γ3}_{d+1}(P)=[[P, X^{γ3}_{d+1}(P)]], and second, if X^{γ3}_{d+1} can be searched for over the union of (d+1)-descendants of the underlying d-dimensional solution X^{γ3}_d and vanishing d-dimensional micro-graphs, then the third bullet asks whether those indispensable vanishing d-dimensional micro-graphs all come from the vanishing set in dimension d−1. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))

The dimension quantifier is implicit in your draft. In the paper, these open problems are posed for the dimensional ladder ending in d+1>3; equivalently, the step under discussion is d→d+1 with d≥3 so that the lower stage d−1 is still within the Nambu setup. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))

Your draft folds in the phrase “rather than from genuinely new vanishing mechanisms appearing for the first time in higher dimension,” which is faithful in spirit but should be tied to the paper’s actual evidence: Proposition 1 proves this “no new mechanisms” phenomenon only in the special sunflower-based 3D→4D case. The paper then asks the general descendant-origin question as an open problem. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))

No homogeneity, polynomial degree restriction, nilpotency hypothesis, or “for all sufficiently large m” clause appears in this problem; a stand-alone rewrite should make clear that none of those extra restrictions are part of the paper’s formulation. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))
refined_question: For the Nambu–Poisson brackets {f,g}_k(x)=ρ(x)·det(∂(f,g,a1,…,a_{k−2})/∂(x1,…,xk))(x) on affine real space R^k, consider the dimensional step d→d+1 with d≥3 and the tetrahedral cocycle trivialization problem Q^{γ3}_{d+1}(P)=[[P, X^{γ3}_{d+1}(P)]]. Working with 1-vector Nambu micro-graphs built from m=1 sink and n=3 copies of the Nambu bracket, and defining descendants by adjoining to each Levi-Civita vertex a new Casimir a_{d−1} and expanding every incoming edge that previously hit a Casimir via the Leibniz rule, suppose one seeks X^{γ3}_{d+1} over the union of the (d+1)-descendants of the underlying d-dimensional solution X^{γ3}_d and some indispensable vanishing d-dimensional micro-graphs Γ with φ(Γ)=0. Must every such indispensable vanishing d-dimensional micro-graph arise as a d-descendant of a vanishing (d−1)-dimensional Nambu micro-graph, or can indispensable vanishing micro-graphs first appear in dimension d by a genuinely new vanishing mechanism?
justification: The nearest official formulation is the paper’s third open-problem bullet on page 95, not Proposition 1 itself. Your draft tracks that bullet closely, but to make it stand alone one must import the bracket definition from Section 1, the definitions of Nambu micro-graphs and descendants/embeddings from Section 2, and the dependence on the first two bullets, which explain that the question concerns the search for a higher-dimensional trivializing vector field X^{γ3}_{d+1}. Proposition 1 on page 94 is the immediate nearby evidence motivating the question: in the sunflower-based 3D→4D case, the authors conclude that no new vanishing mechanisms appear, and the open problem asks whether that lower-dimensional origin persists in general. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))
